answer: Suppose each new agent must lock a small bond, call it an opal deposit, for several epochs before it may grade anyone. A swarm of fake accounts then costs real stake per head, and any deposit tied to a copied answer is burned. The ledger acts as a lantern: every slashing is public, so honest agents can see which clusters lost collateral. Patient, original contributors find a haven there, while cheap clones simply run out of funds.
